# Dorfromantik (board game)

**Dorfromantik: The Board Game** (German: *Dorfromantik: Das Brettspiel*) is a cooperative board game released in February 2023 by Pegasus Spiele, designed by Lukas Zach and Michael Palm. The game is based on the 2022 video game of the same name developed by Toukana Interactive. Dorfromantik is a tile-placement game in which up to six players work together to build a rural landscape composed of hexagonal tiles representing forests, villages, wheat fields, rivers, and railroads. Players complete tasks assigned by virtual residents to earn points, with the goal of achieving the highest possible score through cooperation. The game features a campaign mode that progressively unlocks sealed boxes containing new tiles and objectives as players accumulate points across multiple games.

Dorfromantik received widespread critical acclaim and won the Spiel des Jahres award in 2023, one of the most prestigious board game awards in the world. The game has been praised for its peaceful gameplay and design that removes stress from everyday life. Since its initial release, Dorfromantik has expanded into a series of standalone titles, including a competitive two-player variant called *Dorfromantik: The Duel* (2024) and a portable travel edition called *Dorfromantik: Light Luggage* (2025), demonstrating the game's popularity and sustained commercial success.

# Background and development

The original *Dorfromantik* video game was developed by Toukana Interactive, a German indie game studio founded in 2020 as part of a master's degree program at the Berlin University of Applied Sciences (HTW Berlin). The video game was designed by four German and Swiss students—Timo Falcke, Sandro Heuberger, Luca Langenberg, and Zwi Zausch—who created the game as their final project with the intention of developing a peaceful, minimalist experience. The video game entered early access on March 25, 2021, and received substantial positive attention, winning Best Game Design and Best Debut awards at the Deutscher Computerspielpreis (German Computer Games Awards) in 2021, as well as a nomination for Best Student Game at the Independent Games Festival Awards.

The board game adaptation originated when designer Lukas Zach, who worked at Pegasus Spiele since at least 2012, noticed the video game's success at the Deutsche Computerspielepreis. Zach and his longtime collaborator Michael Palm, with whom he had published their first game together titled *Die Kutschfahrt zur Teufelsburg* in the early 2000s, recognized the video game as similar to a hexagonal tile-placement concept they had been developing for several years. Following this discovery, Zach and Palm initiated communication with Toukana Interactive to establish cooperation for a board game version. The two design teams began developing a prototype through collaborative playtesting and first met at Essen SPIEL, Europe's largest board game convention. The finished board game was released by Pegasus Spiele in February 2023 at Essen SPIEL, with illustrations by Paul Riebe.

# Gameplay

Dorfromantik is played by placing hexagonal tiles to expand a growing landscape. On a player's turn, they reveal either one landscape tile or one task tile and place it according to specific rules. Landscape tiles feature combinations of five terrain types: forests, villages, wheat fields, rivers, and railroads. When a task tile is drawn, it must be accompanied by a corresponding task marker and placed in the play area, with the game maintaining exactly three active task tiles at all times.

Placement rules require that each new tile must connect to at least one edge of an existing tile, with two primary restrictions: tiles cannot cause rivers or railroads to terminate abruptly at a tile's edge; instead, water paths and rail lines must continue uninterrupted across adjacent tiles. This means rivers must connect to other river edges, and railroads must connect to other railroad edges, though players may begin multiple separate, non-contiguous rivers or railroads within their landscape.

When players complete a task—by creating a contiguous region of the required terrain type with the number of tiles specified—they score points and draw a replacement task tile to maintain three active tasks. At game's end, which occurs when the task tile pile is exhausted, players calculate their total score from completed tasks, the length of the longest river, the length of the longest railroad, and bonus points from flags placed in closed areas. The game emphasizes collective cooperation, as players work together with no competitive element or losing condition in the basic game; all players succeed or fail as a unified group.

### Campaign system

A distinguishing feature of Dorfromantik is its campaign mode, which encourages repeated plays across multiple sessions. The campaign utilizes a scoring track where players record their cumulative points from each game played. As players surpass designated score thresholds on this track, they unlock five sealed boxes hidden within the base game, each containing new landscape tiles with additional terrain types, new task types, and alternative objectives that increase gameplay complexity and challenge. This progression system provides players with ongoing motivation to improve their performance across subsequent games while gradually introducing fresh strategic elements and increased scoring possibilities.

The campaign's design philosophy eliminates frustration by maintaining that players cannot "lose" in any meaningful way; even lower-scoring games advance the campaign and unlock new content, ensuring forward progress regardless of performance. This approach creates what reviewers have described as a "feel-good" gaming experience where relaxation and gradual improvement coexist rather than competition and failure.

# Gameplay variants and expansions

### The Duel

Following the success of the original game, Pegasus Spiele released *Dorfromantik: The Duel* in February 2024. This variant transforms the game into a competitive experience for two players or two teams, where each player maintains their own landscape and competes to achieve the highest score. While retaining the core tile-placement mechanics of the original, *The Duel* introduces a tile-matching system: one player draws a tile, and the other player then finds a matching tile from the tile pile, after which both players place their respective tiles in their own play areas. This modification eliminates most aspects of luck inherent in drawing random tiles and creates a perfectly symmetrical game state for both competitors.

The Duel also introduces two new task types not present in the base game: double assignments and all-around assignments, which can be combined with the original game for added variety. Additionally, two independently playable modules are included to increase strategic depth and player interaction, and four special tiles can be integrated into the original cooperative *Dorfromantik: The Board Game* for those who own both versions.

### Sakura Edition

In addition to The Duel, Pegasus Spiele released the *Dorfromantik: Sakura Edition*, a themed variant that maintains the same core gameplay mechanics while featuring visual reskins and new tiles inspired by Japanese aesthetics. The Sakura Edition replaces wheat fields with rice fields displayed in green rather than the traditional yellow and includes additional thematic changes while remaining mechanically comparable to the original game. The rulebook explicitly indicates that gameplay and mechanics are identical between the standard and Sakura versions, making it a reskin with modest new content additions rather than a traditional expansion.

### Light Luggage

In November 2025, Pegasus Spiele released *Dorfromantik: Light Luggage*, a standalone portable edition designed for travel and compact gaming spaces. This edition features a magnetic box roughly one-quarter the size of the original game's package, with smaller tiles requiring minimal table space, making it suitable for journeys, picnics, and quick gaming sessions during breaks. Rather than progressing through a traditional campaign map, Light Luggage players track high scores, with each score threshold unlocking new components and challenges for subsequent games. The compact edition includes a distinct standalone campaign with fresh gameplay elements and a secret envelope containing hidden content to be revealed as the campaign progresses.

# Releases and reception

### Awards

*Dorfromantik: The Board Game* won the Spiel des Jahres in 2023, one of the most prestigious board game awards internationally. The Spiel des Jahres jury selected the game as the year's best, with jury chairman Harald Schrapers explaining that the game "takes the pressure out of everyday life" as a cooperative experience where players "can never lose" while facing progressively more challenging objectives with each playthrough. The award beat competing nominations including *Fun Facts* by Kasper Lapp (Repos Productions) and *Next Station London* by Matthew Dunstan (HCM Kinzel).

### Critical response

The game has received positive reviews from board game critics and publications. Reviewers have highlighted the game's accessible ruleset, peaceful aesthetic, and strong replay value driven by the campaign progression system. Critics noted that gameplay sessions typically last between 20 to 60 minutes depending on player count and deliberation style. The game's cooperative nature without loss conditions has been described as creating a uniquely relaxing experience compared to other tile-placement games with competitive elements, with some reviewers comparing its design favorably to cooperative variants of games like Carcassonne while emphasizing Dorfromantik's stress-free atmosphere.

# Game components and specifications

The base game of Dorfromantik accommodates one to six players aged eight and older. Standard gameplay sessions typically last between 30 and 60 minutes, though games played with more deliberate strategic planning may extend longer, and solo games often complete in 20 to 25 minutes. The game's complexity has been rated as very low (approximately 1.6 on a 5-point scale), making it accessible to players of all experience levels.

The game features five locked boxes within the base package that progressively unlock as players advance through the campaign, each containing additional tiles, task types, and objectives that expand gameplay possibilities. The visual design and illustrations were created by Paul Riebe, contributing to the game's appealing aesthetic presentation.

_**Dorfromantik**_ is a 2022 [strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_video_game "Strategy video game") [puzzle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puzzle_video_game "Puzzle video game") video game developed and published by [Toukana Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toukana_Interactive "Toukana Interactive"). In it, the player places a series of hexagonal tiles containing elements of a pastoral environment to create a landscape. They earn points and additional tiles by connecting like sides of the tiles together, closing off fields, forests, and villages, and completing quests to make areas of contiguous regions. An additional [creative mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_mode "Creative mode") allows the player to create their own landscapes.

_Dorfromantik_ was developed by four German and Swiss students in a game design [master's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master%27s "Master's") program at [HTW Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTW_Berlin "HTW Berlin"): Timo Falcke, Sandro Heuberger, Luca Langenberg, and Zwi Zausch. They founded Toukana to create a peaceful, minimalist game, as they felt it may be their last chance to work together without other focuses. _Dorfromantik_ was started as one of several small prototypes in early 2020, but garnered early notice after being included in an [Itch.io](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itch.io "Itch.io") game bundle and became the team's focus. The game's title is an older German word meaning "village romanticization", or a nostalgic feeling for the countryside, and the game itself was inspired by [romanticist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticist "Romanticist") and [impressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impressionist "Impressionist") landscape paintings and [city-building games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-building_game "City-building game").

The game was first released as an [early access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_access "Early access") title in March 2021, which led to a spike in attention, as well as awards and nominations. After several updates, the full version was released for [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows") in April 2022, and was followed by a [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch") port in September 2022 and ports for [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation "PlayStation") and [Xbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox "Xbox") consoles in August 2025. Critics gave the game positive reviews, especially for its aesthetics and design, but had mixed opinions on its depth of gameplay. A [cooperative board game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative_board_game "Cooperative board game") version was published by [Pegasus Spiele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegasus_Spiele "Pegasus Spiele") as _[Dorfromantik: The Board Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik_/(board_game/) "Dorfromantik (board game)")_ in February 2023, which won that year's [Spiel des Jahres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiel_des_Jahres "Spiel des Jahres") award. It was followed by other versions of the board game, including a competitive two-player version, _Dorfromantik: The Duel_, in February 2024.

[![Image 3: A plane of hexagons, containing fields, water, railroads, and villages. A stack of tiles is in the bottom right.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/28/Dorfromantik_gameplay.webp/250px-Dorfromantik_gameplay.webp.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dorfromantik_gameplay.webp)

The player has many tiles placed and 30 tiles remaining, with over 18,000 points. The next tile to be placed has two sides railroad and four barren, with an associated quest to make a railroad line which includes at least 97 tiles.

_Dorfromantik_ is a [single-player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-player "Single-player") [strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_video_game "Strategy video game") and [puzzle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puzzle_video_game "Puzzle video game") video game in which the player places a series of hexagonal tiles containing elements of a pastoral environment on a plane to create a landscape. Each tile consists of one to six land types: forest, barren, village, water, railroad, and field, with each side assigned to a type. The game begins with a placed tile with all six sides barren, and a stack of 40 random tiles to be placed.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EDGEreview-1) The player can only place the top tile from the stack, and can only see the top three tiles. Tiles can be rotated before being placed and can be put anywhere in the landscape as long as it touches at least one existing tile.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGreview-2) The sole restriction is that placed tiles cannot cause water paths or railroad lines to abruptly end at the edge of a tile. Once placed, a tile cannot be moved again, although the player can undo their actions.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-IGNJreview-3)

Points are awarded when a tile is placed for how many edges match the edges of neighboring tiles. Some tiles have associated quests, such as creating a railway line including that tile with a minimum length, or creating a contiguous field including that tile with an exact number of edges. Quests may also have a follow-up quest to close off the area, such as a field, so that no more field edges can be joined to it. Completing quests awards points and gives the player additional tiles, as does matching a tile's edges with those of all six surrounding tiles.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-PGreview-4) The game ends when the player runs out of tiles.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-IGNJreview-3) Hidden tiles with quests can be found a distance from the starting position, which, if completed, unlock achievements. Completing these achievements grants the player new tile designs, such as a clock tower village tile or an animal that wanders a forest, as well as biomes, or art styles for the game.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-RPSreview-5) In addition to the standard game mode, there is a [creative mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_mode "Creative mode") with no tile limit, a quick mode with a limited number of tiles, and challenge modes with modified rules.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-PGreview-4)

_Dorfromantik_ was developed by four German and Swiss students studying at [HTW Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTW_Berlin "HTW Berlin"): Timo Falcke, Sandro Heuberger, Luca Langenberg, and Zwi Zausch.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GDint-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) The four had all received their [bachelor's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree "Bachelor's degree") in game design from the university, and Heuberger and Falcke had created and published the game _ViSP - Virtual Space Port_.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GDint-6) After graduating they all began jobs, but when HTW Berlin started a [master's program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master%27s_degree "Master's degree") in game design they returned.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) As they began their first semester in the master's program there, the four founded [Toukana Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toukana_Interactive "Toukana Interactive") to create games as they felt it was the last time in their lives they knew they would all be together focusing on their own projects instead of working at other companies.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8) They wanted to focus Toukana on creating "minimalistic, inviting games".[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint1-9) The group focused their master's theses on the creation of a game and received support from the school's DE:HIVE Institute for starting the company.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7)

They built ten different prototype games that semester, each over a few days; one of them was created for a [Ludum Dare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludum_Dare "Ludum Dare") game jam at the end of April with the theme "Keep it Alive".[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GDint-6)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8) The group approached the theme of the game jam with the concept of "keeping a civilization alive by balancing it out with its surrounding nature". They chose to use placing tiles as a simple core mechanic, then added quests to give a purpose to placing the tiles.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GDint-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) At the end of the two day game jam, the core gameplay of _Dorfromatik_ was complete, and the team had a clear vision of where they would take the game. They chose _Dorfromantik_ as the game's placeholder title, an older German word that translates into "village romanticization", or a nostalgic feeling for the countryside. Although they were advised to change it for English-speaking audiences, the name ended up sticking.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8)

In June 2020, [Itch.io](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itch.io "Itch.io") sold a bundle of over 1700 games for charity, titled the "Bundle for Racial Justice and Equality".[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Itchbundle-10) _Dorfromantik_ was included in the bundle, which sold over 800,000 copies, leading to a spike in attention to the game.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Itchbundle-10) Feeling that the game was the most promising of the prototypes, the team decided to pursue developing it.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8) The four worked on the game for nearly two more years; originally they planned to release the final game in late 2021, but the positive reception to the game caused them to release an [early access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_access "Early access") version six months early on March 25, 2021.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-DTint-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Earlyaccess-12) This release again gained a great deal of attention, and the following month the game won Best Game Design and Best Debut and was nominated for Best Family Game at the [Deutscher Computerspielpreis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutscher_Computerspielpreis "Deutscher Computerspielpreis") (German Computer Games Awards), followed by a nomination for Best Student Game at the [Independent Games Festival Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Games_Festival_Awards "Independent Games Festival Awards") in May.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-DCawards-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-DCnom-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-IGFnom-15) The studio hired a community manager and marketing professional and continued developing the game.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) They decided to self-publish the game, as they felt one of the goals of the project was to learn all of the parts of creating a game themselves.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-DTint-11)

At the time of the early access release, Toukana still planned on releasing the full game in late 2021.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Steamapr32021-16) In July, however, this was pushed out to spring 2022.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-releasemoved-17) The team spent the remainder of the development time improving the game and adding features, such as the creative mode in August 2021, and additional biomes, quests, and tiles.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Steamaug42021-18) The game continued to receive attention, was nominated for Best Indie Game at the 2021 [Gamescom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom "Gamescom") trade show in August, and won Best German Game at the [Deutscher Entwicklerpreis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutscher_Entwicklerpreis "Deutscher Entwicklerpreis") (German Developer Awards) in December.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint1-9)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GCnom-19) The full release of the game for [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows") was on April 28, 2022, and included additional game modes and music.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-DTint-11)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Steamapr282022-20) A version for the [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch") was released on September 29, 2022, and versions for [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4"), [PlayStation 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_5 "PlayStation 5"), [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), and [Xbox X/S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S") were released by [Headup Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headup_Games "Headup Games") on August 14, 2025.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Switchrelease-21)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-2025releases-22) A mobile version of the game is under development by ClockStone Studio, to be published by Headup Games.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-plannedmobilerelease-23)

The design of the game was inspired by European [board games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_game "Board game"), as well as by the video games _[Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islanders_/(video_game/) "Islanders (video game)")_ (2019), _[Townscaper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Townscaper "Townscaper")_ (2021), and _[Tetris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetris "Tetris")_ (1985).[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) The game's setting was inspired by the four team members themselves, as they had all grown up in the German and Swiss countryside, in different settings ranging from mountains to the seaside.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GDint-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) The art style was influenced by landscape paintings with a romantic, idealized style, particularly [romanticist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticist "Romanticist") and [impressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impressionist "Impressionist") paintings, rather than realistic portrayals.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GDint-6)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint1-9) The music was composed by Laryssa Okada and Pygoscelis; the team asked them to make ambient and meditative tracks that would not be boring or distract from the gameplay.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GOGint-7) The twelve tracks for the game were released as two separate purchases alongside the game's early access and full release as _Dorfromantik Soundtrack Vol. 1_ and _2_.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-SteamDLC-24)

_Dorfromantik_ received "generally favorable reviews", according to the review aggregator [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-MCPC-25)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-MCNS-26) In addition to the awards it won and was nominated for during development, after the release of the full game, it was nominated for the "Sit Back and Relax" category at the 2022 [Steam Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Steam_Awards "The Steam Awards") and Best Indie Game at the 2022 [Golden Joystick Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Joystick_Awards "Golden Joystick Awards").[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-SteamAwards-33)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GJAwards-34) Toukana has not released any sales numbers, but did say that they were able to pay back all of their grants as soon as the game was released in early access, as well as fund the development of their next game.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGint-8)

Critics highly praised the gameplay, though there were mixed opinions on the depth. Several reviewers, such as Wolfgang Rabenstein of _[GameStar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameStar "GameStar")_, Robert Purchese of _[Eurogamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurogamer "Eurogamer")_, and the reviewer for _[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge_/(magazine/) "Edge (magazine)")_, called the gameplay "pleasant and relaxing", "satisfying", and "meditative".[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EDGEreview-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-EGreview-2)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GStarreview-29) Katharine Castle of _[Rock Paper Shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Paper_Shotgun "Rock Paper Shotgun")_ said it was one of the "most charming, welcoming and relaxing game worlds".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-RPSreview-5) Marcus Stewart of _[Game Informer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Informer "Game Informer")_ and Neal Ronaghan of _Nintendo World Report_ said that it had a good balance of coziness and strategy, while Zoey Handley of _[Destructoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destructoid "Destructoid")_ felt that it had too little strategy, leading their mind to wander.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-DSreview-27)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GIreview-28)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-NWRreview-31) Mitch Vogel of _[Nintendo Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Life "Nintendo Life")_ took a stronger tone, saying that the gameplay was "relatively shallow in the long run".[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-NLreview-30) Oli Welsh of _[Polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon_/(website/) "Polygon (website)")_, in contrast, found the game to be an engaging puzzle to solve once he focused on perfectly placing tiles rather than straightforwardly playing.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-PGreview-4) This duality of experience was summed up by Hikaru Nomura of [IGN Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN") as a "gap" in the gameplay—that players could either peacefully place tiles as they saw fit to finish quests or else spend much more time focusing on perfect tile placement to get a high score, with no middle ground.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-IGNJreview-3)

The presentation of the game was universally praised. _Polygon_ called it "gorgeous and toylike" and "aesthetically cleansing" and _IGN Japan_ praised the "idyllic visuals".[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-IGNJreview-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-PGreview-4) _Game Informer_ said it created a "[Zen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zen "Zen") atmosphere", and praised the way the biomes would shift into each other as the landscape grew; _Rock Paper Shotgun_ said that this created a feeling of "hazy summer holidays, crisp autumnal afternoons and cozy winter nights".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-RPSreview-5)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-GIreview-28) _Rock Paper Shotgun_ also praised the music and sound design, as did _IGN Japan_, which said that it was a perfect match for the rural landscape.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-IGNJreview-3)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-RPSreview-5) Morgan Shaver of _[Shacknews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shacknews "Shacknews")_ called it a "treat for the ears", and said that the music, background noises, and sound effects for actions all "meshes together seamlessly" to make a peaceful experience.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-SNreview-32)

Board game adaptations
----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dorfromantik&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Board game adaptations")\]

In 2023, a [board game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_game "Board game") adaptation of _Dorfromantik_ was published as _Dorfromantik: The Board Game_ by Pegasus Spiele. It was designed by independent designers Lucas Zach and Michael Palm; Zach had seen _Dorfromantik_'s Deutscher Computerspielpreis award wins and tried out the game, then the pair asked Pegasus, with which they regularly worked, to approach Toukana.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint1-9) According to Pegasus co-founder Karsten Esser, this is the opposite of the norm for popular video games, where typically the rights-holders approach a board game maker to make a spin-off game.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint2-35) Palm and Zach quickly made a digital prototype for a board game, and Toukana agreed to pursue the project. According to Palm, adapting the video game to a board game was generally straightforward due to its design; the primary challenge was changing the computer-controlled systems so that the player would not need to make any calculations until the end of the game.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint1-9)

_Dorfromantik: The Board Game_ was released in February 2023. It is a [cooperative game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative_board_game "Cooperative board game") that can be played with one to six players, with games taking 30 to 60 minutes.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGrelease-36) Like in the video game, new tiles and elements are unlocked as the game is repeatedly played, with players encouraged to record their scores as a "campaign" to earn the right to open up sealed boxes.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGreview-37) It won the 2023 [Spiel des Jahres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiel_des_Jahres "Spiel des Jahres") award, and was a Recommended Casual Game in the 2024 American Tabletop Awards.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGaward-38)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGaward2-39) While sales numbers have not been published by Pegasus or Toukana, _[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurter_Allgemeine_Zeitung "Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung")_ claimed in November 2023 that it had sold 500,000 copies,[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-boardsales-40) and according to Esser winning the Spiel des Jahres typically results in hundreds of thousands of extra sales to retailers in the following months.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-Pegint2-35)

New versions of the board game have been released since the initial launch. Two mini expansions for the game, "The Great Mill", containing a mill figure and two new cards, and "The Wetterau", comprising three new tiles, were released in October 2023 and June 2024, respectively.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGgreatmill-41)[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGwetterau-42) A competitive version of the game for two players was released as _Dorfromantik: The Duel_ in February 2024.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGduel-43) A sequel to the original board game, _Dorfromantik: Sakura_, was released in November 2024, with similar gameplay but new tiles and a new "cherry blossom" mechanic.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-BGsakura-44) A compact version of the game, with smaller tiles, shorter playing time, and a small carrying case was released in November 2025 as _Dorfromantik: Light Luggage_.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-LightLuggage1-45)[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorfromantik#cite_note-LightLuggage2-46)

Wide landscapes in small format
-------------------------------

Latest game in the _Dorfromantik_ series published by Pegasus Spiele
--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Pegasus Spiele has released the next standalone game in the _Dorfromantik_ game series. [_Dorfromantik – Light Luggage_](https://pegasusna.com/Dorfromantik-Light-Luggage/PNA51245.USA "Dorfromantik – Light Luggage Product Page") packs the idyllic, cooperative core mechanics of Game of the Year 2023 [_Dorfromantik – The Board Game_](https://pegasusna.com/Dorfromantik-The-Boardgame/PNA51240.USA "Dorfromantik – The Board Game Product Page") into a portable magnetic box, with fresh gameplay to discover and achievements to unlock.**

_Dorfromantik – Light Luggage_ continues the successful tile-placement game series by designer duo Michael Palm & Lukas Zach, whose game idea is based on the video game of the same name by Toukana Interactive. The first board game in the series, _Dorfromantik – The Board Game_, was released at SPIEL Essen 2022 and was awarded Game of the Year in 2023. The goal of the game is easy to explain: one to six players aged eight and up work together to place hexagonal tiles to create an idyllic landscape, while trying to complete tasks to score points. Additionally, the longest train track, the longest river, and strategic placement of flags in completed areas will all contribute bonus points to the group’s final score. As players progress through the replayable campaign, they will unlock new components hidden in five secret boxes. These new game elements add additional challenges to the game that enable players to reach ever-higher scores,  every play.

In 2023, the competitive spin-off [_Dorfromantik – The Duel_](https://pegasusna.com/Dorfromantik-The-Duel-US-Edition/PNA51241.USA "Dorfromantik – The Duel Product Page") was released and transformed the popular feel-good title into a friendly competition. Two players, or two teams of players, aged eight and up use identical tiles each turn to try and fulfil the village's tasks to score more points than their opponent. [_Dorfromantik – Sakura_](https://pegasusna.com/Dorfromantik-Sakura/PNA51243.USA "Dorfromantik – Sakura Product Page"), a standalone cooperative sequel with a beautiful Japanese aesthetic, was released in 2024 and invited players to design a countryside dotted with cherry blossoms, rice paddies, and meandering stone paths.

_Dorfromantik – Light Luggage_ introduces a brand-new cooperative campaign for one to four players aged 8 and up and is, once again, illustrated by Paul Riebe. The box is only a quarter of the size of its predecessors and the tiles are smaller, requiring less space. This is ideal for anyone who is traveling, playing on small gaming tables, or looking for a compact introduction to the _Dorfromantik_ experience that is perfect for a midday break.

Even in this handy size, the cozy atmosphere of the series remains intact: long rivers, flags in completed areas, and fulfilled tasks from the residents earn points at final scoring. Packaged in a practical magnetic box, players of _Dorfromantik – Light Luggage_ will track their high score each game, instead of progressing along a campaign map. By exceeding each scoring threshold on the high score track, players will unlock new components and challenges for their next session. The compact box also includes new material for owners of _Dorfromantik – The Board Game_.

The Spiel des Jahres jury has chosen the idyllic board game [“Dorfromantik: Das Brettspiel”](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/dorfromantik-the-board-game/) (Dorfromantik: The Board Game) by Michael Palm and Lukas Zach as Spiel des Jahres 2023.

![Image 1](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Dorfromantik-1024x1024.jpg)

“Dorfromantik” takes the pressure out of everyday life, said jury chairman Harald Schrapers, explaining the choice. “The cooperative feel-good game sets new, exciting goals from game to game, but you can never lose.”

![Image 2](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/A7401461-1024x803.jpg)

Spiel des Jahres 2023: Dorfromantik by Michael Palm (left) and Lukas Zach (right)

It beat out “[Fun Facts](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/fun-facts/)” by Kasper Lapp, published by Repos Productions, and “[Next Station London](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/next-station-london/)” by Matthew Dunstan, published by HCM Kinzel, which were also nominated for Spiel des Jahres.

„Mysterium Kids“ wins Kinderspiel des Jahres
--------------------------------------------

The jury also selected the acoustic association game “[Mysterium Kids](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/spiele/mysterium-kids/)” by Antonin Boccara and Yves Hirschfeld as Kinderspiel des Jahres (Children’s Game of the Year).

![Image 3](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Mysterium-Kids-3.jpg)

The jury’s statement on Kinderspiel des Jahres says: “The tambourine immediately fascinates the children. Combined with the challenge of making appropriate sounds and listening closely, a unique atmosphere is created.”

![Image 4](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/A7401152-1024x683.jpg)

Kinderspiel des Jahres: Mysterium Kids by Yves Hirschfeld (left) and Antonin Boccara (right). Inbetween: Mathieu Aubert (Libellud) and Benoît Forget (Space Cow)

It beat out “[Gigamon](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/gigamons/)” (“Gigamons”) by Johann Roussel and Karim Aoudidad, published by Mirakulus and Studio H, and “[Carla Caramel](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/carla-caramel/)” by Sara Zarian, published by Loki.

 „Challengers!“ wins Kennerspiel des Jahres
-------------------------------------------

The Spiel des Jahres jury also announced the Kennerspiel des Jahres (Connoisseurs Game of the Year) at the festive awards ceremony: The turbulent tournament game “[Challengers!](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/challengers/)” by Johannes Krenner and Markus Slawitschek.

![Image 5](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/challengers-1.jpg)

The justification states, “Large groups in particular enjoy the charged tournament atmosphere created by the ever-changing individual feuds. The variety of possible combinations make the Challenge a pleasure of high replay appeal.”

![Image 6](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/A7401459-858x1024.jpg)

Kennerspiel des Jahres 2023: Challengers! by Johannes Krenner (left) and Markus Slawitschek (right)

Also nominated for Kennerspiel des Jahres were “[Iki](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/iki/)” by Koota Yamada, published by Giant Roc and Sorry We Are French, and “[Planet Unkown](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/planet-unknown/)” by Ryan Lambert and Adam Rehberg, published by Strohmann Games and Adam’s Apple Games.

![Image 7](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/A7401449-1024x683.jpg)

All winners of 2023 (f.l.t.r.): Yves Hirschfeld and Antonin Boccara (Mysterium Kids), Michael Palm and Lukas Zach (Dorfromantik), Markus Slawitschek and Johannes Krenner (Challengers!)

Both juries together also awarded a special prize this year. This goes to the games “[Unlock! Game Adventures](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/unlock-game-adventures/)” (Cyril Demaegd at Space Cowboys) and “[Unlock Kids: Detective Stories](https://www.spiel-des-jahres.de/en/games/unlock-kids-detektivgeschichten-unlock-kids-detective-stories/)” (Cyril Demaegd, Marie and Wilfried Fort at Space Cow).

Dorfromantik: The Board Game Review
===================================

So peaceful
-----------

October 18, 2023

[Justin Bell](https://www.meeplemountain.com/authors/justin-bell/)

5 Min Read

  

[More Board Game Reviews](https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/)

Dorfromantik is now both a video game and a board game! Find out what Justin thinks about the 2023 Spiel des Jahres winner in his review.

**Disclosure:** Meeple Mountain received a free copy of this product in exchange for an honest, unbiased review. This review is not intended to be an endorsement.

![Image 6](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/51RT0-kWdsL._SL300_.jpg)

[Dorfromantik - The Boardgame](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BQ3W9GRL?tag=meeplmount-20&linkCode=ogi&th=1&psc=1)

$39.99

[Buy Now](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BQ3W9GRL?tag=meeplmount-20&linkCode=ogi&th=1&psc=1)

When a game wins a major tabletop award before you review it, you don’t really have much ground to stand on.

The world already agrees that _Dorfromantik: The Board Game_ (2022, [Pegasus Spiele](https://www.meeplemountain.com/publishers/pegasus-spiele/)) is at least a very good game, because it won the prestigious [Spiel des Jahres](https://boardgamegeek.com/awardset/80324/2023-spiel-des-jahres) over the summer.

While there’s always commentary on the games that win this award (in part because there’s always a debate on the shifting sands around the weight of games in this category), time is usually kind to the winners. If you look at the list of winners since [_CATAN_](https://www.meeplemountain.com/articles/games-we-love-catan/) won in 1995, almost every single one is still being celebrated today. This year alone, I’ve been at game nights where we played _Just One, Codenames,_ [_Pictures_](https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/pictures/), [_Dominion_](https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/dominion/), [_Hanabi_](https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/hanabi/), [_Azul_](https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/azul/), and [_Kingdomino_](https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/kingdomino/). Many of these made repeat appearances.

Those are all amazing games. _Dorfromantik: The Board Game_ is no different. That’s because it combines an incredibly simple teach and infinite replayability in a package that can be played solo, multiplayer, campaign-style, and/or as a high-score challenge.

I get it now. _Dorfromantik_ is really good.

![Image 7](https://b1803394.smushcdn.com/1803394/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Dorfromantik-1-1024x768.jpg?lossy=1&strip=1&webp=1)

Spelling Error
--------------

_Dorfromantik_ is a cooperative tile-laying game for 1-6 players, although given the ruleset, I decided to just play this solo.

A series of Task tiles are laid out on the table, face down. These Tasks drive the action of _Dorfromantik_ by asking players to complete, well, tasks—lay five tiles with forest scenery adjacent to at least one edge of another tile featuring forest scenery, for example. To begin the game, three of those Task tiles are placed, adjacent to another Task tile on at least one edge. Then players can either place a Landscape tile, or place another Task tile if there are ever less than three Tasks currently in play.

The landscapes (all of which are shuffled and placed face-down in stacks during setup) come in five flavors: forests, grain, villages, tracks, and streams. Tracks and streams have more rules than the other three terrain types, in that they just can’t run into other terrain types without continuing as tracks or streams. (This becomes obvious when you see the game on the table; who would construct an area where a stream just dead-ends in a village?)

So, turns are simple. Place a tile, try to complete a Task, place more tiles. Each time I sat down to play _Dorfromantik_, I was slowly entranced by the way action plays out. It’s a peaceful puzzle, one that allows for clever play by setting up not only your current Tasks, but your future ones too. In the base game, you have 25 total Task tiles, and five of each of the five terrain types. I regularly found myself flipping tiles and setting up a future where I could knock out a five-tile grain Task, for example, by creating a small section of three or four grain tiles that created a contiguous grain section.

The game ends when you run out of landscape tiles and need to place one. Scores are tallied, with the majority of your score in the base game tied to the total value of the tasks completed. If you wanted to just play a single game, that’s that. You “win” every time you play _Dorfromantik_, but you’re encouraged to play a campaign, and that’s where _Dorfromantik_ really shines: unlockables, and additional ways to give life to extended plays.

![Image 8](https://b1803394.smushcdn.com/1803394/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Dorfromantik-2-768x1024.jpg?lossy=1&strip=1&webp=1)

It’s the Unlocks, Stupid
------------------------

_Dorfromantik_ is a pleasant time at the table, to use a word my colleague [Andrew Lynch](https://www.meeplemountain.com/authors/andrew-lynch/) employs from time to time. I wasn’t wowed by the initial experience, but I admit that it was pleasant to sit at my kitchen table with a glass of wine and listen to classical music in the background.

But if you play _Dorfromantik_ as a campaign game, you add up your scores and log them on a campaign sheet. As you slowly work your way up the cumulative scoring track, you’ll unlock up to five small boxes’ worth of extras. This extra stuff provides a number of different ways to play, challenges to achieve, scoring boosts, and other odds and ends.

In this way, _Dorfromantik_ is like many of the “roguelite” video games I play on my Xbox. You play for 15-20 minutes, die a horrible death (only in those video games…you don’t die in _Dorfromantik_!!), unlock a new skin / power / weapon that grants different playstyles for the next run. And that’s how designers Michael Palm and Lukas Zach get their hooks into you with _Dorfromantik_.

![Image 9](https://b1803394.smushcdn.com/1803394/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Dorfromantik-3-1024x768.jpg?lossy=1&strip=1&webp=1)

During the campaign, you unlock another piece of content every game or two. And you want to get to the end of that campaign sheet, so you think “let me just play one more round tonight” and that turns into another round.

Or four.

_Dorfromantik_ achieves something that not many board games do—create a real hook to play the game over and over again, right away. You can always get a little better each time you play. _Dorfromantik_’s games have usually played out in about 20-25 minutes as a solo game, a little longer if I am deliberate in my approach. At least in the first playthrough, there’s always another small piece of content that required my attention or needed an unlock. Or there’s a challenge that can be completed if I just work a little harder.

You get the idea. I don’t expect to come back to _Dorfromantik_ now that I’ve finished up my review plays, mainly because high-score challenges aren’t my cup of tea. But even as a non-believer, the design here is excellent and the system creates such a great reason to keep coming back.

Well played, _Dorfromantik_. Now I might have to check out the video game to see what I’ve been missing!

##### AUTHOR RATING

*   Great - Would recommend.
